doc.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Bookie's studio, bands and downtown clubs
title: Bradley's without drums and the Woodstock trio
summary: Bradley promised Cobb the drum chair; Cobb played trio with Warren Bernhardt and Dave Holland.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: He told me, he said that even though it was a place you couldn’t play – you only could play bass and piano in there. You couldn’t have no drums, because of a residential thing. He used to tell me, he said, “Soon as I get the drums, you’re the first guy I want to have to play the drums.” So I say, “Yeah, okay.” At that time, I figured that we could have done it, because I was working with a trio up in Woodstock. It was – you know who I’m talking about – it was Warren Bernhardt and . . .
. . . Dave Holland. Warren Bernhardt and Dave Holland. We did some trio stuff up there. You know Warren Bernhardt?

We used to do some trios. So I was telling Sarah, I got just the trio for us, when we do it. But it never happened. I think the first one to do it was probably my man – he used to live right across the street from me. You know who I’m talking – used to play with Monk.
Ben Riley. I think Ben Riley was the first one to do it.
